title: The Trojan Room Coffee Pot (1991)
voice_direction: Dry, amused, unhurried; matter-of-fact on the hook, a small smile on 'a pot they would never taste', brisk on the sale, last question almost deadpan.
narration: This coffee pot should never have been watched by the world. In nineteen ninety-one, computer scientists at Cambridge pointed a camera at one. People on other floors kept climbing the stairs to find it empty. So a cable and a frame grabber put the pot on their screens. The picture was greyscale, only one hundred twenty-eight pixels square. In November nineteen ninety-three, it went onto the web, and anyone with a browser could check a pot they would never taste. The camera was switched off on the twenty-second of August, two thousand one. That month, a Krups machine from its later years sold on eBay for three thousand three hundred fifty pounds. The buyer was Spiegel Online. It was not the original pot. Genius, or just avoiding the stairs?

instagram_caption:
This coffee pot should never have been watched by the world. ☕

In 1991, computer scientists at Cambridge pointed a camera at a coffee pot in the Computer Laboratory. Coffee club members on other floors kept climbing the stairs to find it empty.

The camera fed a frame grabber in an Acorn Archimedes, and a program put a small greyscale image of the pot on their screens. It updated about three times a minute.

In November 1993 the picture went onto the web. The camera was switched off on 22 August 2001.

That month a Krups coffee machine from the pot's later years sold on eBay for £3,350 to Spiegel Online. It was not the original pot. The coffee maker shown is a stand-in, and the lab photo is from 2005.

question: Genius, or just avoiding the stairs?
answer: Genius. Solving a tiny annoyance with a camera and a cable is how half the internet started.

facts.claim: Built 1991 at the Cambridge Computer Laboratory by Quentin Stafford-Fraser and Paul Jardetzky; 128x128 greyscale camera, capture card in an Acorn Archimedes
facts.source: Wikipedia 'Trojan Room coffee pot' citing Stafford-Fraser

facts.claim: Reason: coffee club members on other floors climbed several flights of stairs, often wasted if the pot was already emptied; image updated ~3 times a minute, greyscale
facts.source: Stafford-Fraser, The Trojan Room Coffee Pot (1995)

facts.claim: Put on the web Nov 1993 by Daniel Gordon and Martyn Johnson
Camera switched off 09:54 UTC 22 Aug 2001 after the lab moved to the William Gates Building
Krups ProAroma sold on eBay for £3,350 to Spiegel Online; not the original pot, but the longest-serving, on the web Oct 1997 to Mar 2001; article 13 Aug 2001
Narration says 'that month' for the sale: article dated 13 Aug 2001, auction in Aug 2001; exact end date not checked
